extraction.name: arabic-img2md
extraction.description: A synthetic dataset of 13.7k paired samples of Arabic book pages and their Markdown representations, created using HTML scraped from the Hindawi website for Arabic OCR training and evaluation.
extraction.creator: Mohamed A. Rashad
extraction.rai:dataCollection: The primary training dataset was created by scraping HTML content from the Hindawi website, converting it to PDFs, and extracting Markdown text to form paired samples of Arabic book pages and their Markdown representations.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: HTML content from the Hindawi website, used to generate Arabic book pages and Markdown representations; additionally, over 8,500 books were used to extract 1.1 billion Arabic tokens.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Synthetic paired labels were generated by scraping HTML from the Hindawi website, converting it to PDFs, and extracting Markdown text to create page-Markdown pairs.
extraction.rai:annotationsPerItem: One paired Markdown representation per Arabic book page.
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: HTML scraping, PDF conversion, and Markdown extraction were used to automatically generate annotations.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The paper notes challenges in Arabic OCR related to the language's cursive script, contextual letter forms, and diverse text layouts, and indicates the dataset is synthetic and created from HTML scraped from the Hindawi website.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The dataset and models are intended to support Arabic OCR research and downstream NLP tasks by enabling structured extraction from Arabic books and providing a large Arabic text resource.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: The dataset is used for training and evaluation of Arabic OCR/document parsing models, and the extracted large-scale Arabic text dataset is intended for downstream NLP tasks.
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The models and datasets are open-sourced and implementation is released on GitHub.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Synthetic training pairs were created by scraping HTML content from the Hindawi website, converting it to PDFs, and extracting Markdown text.
